description:
The `releases` table has UNIQUE (profile_id, git_commit_hash, channel). When an attempt fails at any step after the release row insert (steps 3-9 of the orchestrator), the failed row stays in place. Retrying with the same commit+channel hits the unique constraint and returns a generic DB error. Operator workaround today is to delete the failed row manually, which is brittle and undocumented.

Scope of work:
- Change releases/repo.go Insert to handle the case where an existing row on (profile_id, git_commit_hash, channel) has terminal-failure status (failed, verify_failed). Option A: delete the prior row and its release_platforms inside the same transaction, then insert. Option B: update the prior row in place with a new release_id (potentially problematic if downstream stored the old one). Option C: partial unique index WHERE status NOT IN ('failed', 'verify_failed'). Workshop decides.
- Whichever option is chosen, preserve full history in a side table or audit log so a failed release isn't silently discarded.
- Handler-level: ensure retry path is atomic under the advisory lock.
- Tests: two sequential `releases start` calls for the same commit+channel, first fails, second succeeds; UNIQUE violation on an active (pending/publishing/published) release still rejects cleanly.

Out of scope:
- Retrying a partially-succeeded release mid-flight (e.g., one platform published, two failed) — that's a separate orchestrator-resumption concern.
- Bulk cleanup of existing failed rows — workshop decides whether a migration is needed or if rows just organically get replaced on next retry.
name: deployment-manager-release-retry-ergonomics
title: Make releases start Retryable After A Failed Attempt
